theater: 安納托利亞西部與愛琴海東岸

battle.name: 阿爾薩瓦起義
battle.theater: 安納托利亞西部與愛琴海東岸
battle.brief: 前1315年前後，安納托利亞西部的阿爾薩瓦聯盟起兵，抗拒赫梯對礦區、兵員與商路的宗主徵調，戰線落在愛琴海東岸的山地與谷地之間。這場衝突沒有留下戰報，只能由赫梯詩篇與烏加里特泥板回推。卡面月牙劍是埃及的舊式彎刃，屬於同一個東地中海武備圈，而非這片戰場的主力。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 阿爾薩瓦起義的交戰方，一方是安納托利亞西部的阿爾薩瓦及其聯盟城邦，另一方是要求它繼續效忠的赫梯王國。關於阿爾薩瓦，可確定的部分有限，但可以確定其名號在青銅時代晚期是一個西部安納托利亞的政權名，而不是單一城邦：它至少包括愛琴海沿岸的若干港市、山谷中的農業聚落，以及控制內陸礦區的據點；首府一般認為在阿帕薩（今以弗所一帶），哈帕拉則是它最常被提及的另一座城。聯盟的形式是鬆散的，平日各城邦名義上向赫梯納貢，只有遇上共同訴求時才並肩作戰。赫梯方面由老王國的王室直轄：哈圖西里一世在位時曾遠征西部，把阿爾薩瓦壓回附庸地位；到了卡爾納克的年代與前1315年前後，赫梯的西部邊境由王室的軍官與附庸的守備隊分層控制，遠征軍則由國王臨時召集。第三方是烏加里特與阿穆魯這些沿海城邦，它們與阿爾薩瓦既有通商往來，也有邊境糾紛，同時對赫梯與埃及兩面示好，是各方都想拉攏的中介。
countriesEn: The two sides in the Arzawa uprising were, on one hand, Arzawa and the city-states of its alliance in western Anatolia, and on the other the Hittite kingdom, which demanded that it continue to acknowledge its overlordship. What can be established about Arzawa is limited, but it is certain that in the Late Bronze Age the name denoted a political entity in western Anatolia rather than a single city: it included a number of ports along the Aegean coast, agricultural settlements in the valleys, and sites commanding the inland mines; its capital is generally taken to have been Apasa, in the neighbourhood of Ephesus, while Hapala is the other town most often named in connection with it. The alliance was loose: in peacetime the individual city-states nominally paid tribute to Hatti and only fought as one when they had a common grievance. On the Hittite side the command was the royal house's own: Hattusili I had campaigned in the west in his day and forced Arzawa back into the position of a vassal; by the time of the Karnak age and the years around 1315 BC the western frontier was held in layers by royal officers and the garrisons of the vassals, with the field army raised ad hoc by the king. A third party was made up of Ugarit and Amurru, the coastal states that both traded with Arzawa and quarrelled with it over the frontier and that paid their respects to Hatti and to Egypt alike; they were intermediaries every side wanted to draw over.
people: 阿爾薩瓦這個名字在文獻裡主要以國王的名號出現，能辨認的個人極少。可以確定的是赫梯老王國的哈圖西里一世：正是在他的遠征詩《解脫之歌》裡，哈帕拉被攻破，阿爾薩瓦的聯盟與阿蘇瓦諸部族的聯合被寫了下來，這首詩至今是還原這條起義傳統的主要文本；他的前任穆瓦塔里一世則把王國的力量耗在東方與胡里安人的戰線上。另一端是烏加里特的諸王，其中雅卡魯姆的名字見於前13世紀末的王宮信件，他以書寫向赫梯與阿爾薩瓦兩邊陳情；信中同時提到阿赫伊瓦——邁錫尼人的王國——以及阿爾薩瓦的國王，這說明起義的一方並非孤軍。埃及方面，這時在位的是前1319至前1294年的霍倫希布，其後才是塞提一世；埃及的注意力正放在迦南與西奈，新王國早期尚未把軍力遠推到安納托利亞西岸。學界至今仍在爭論阿爾薩瓦的核心地帶究竟在伊茲密、以弗所，還是赫米斯河上游，這場爭論本身就是這場起義留下最多線索的地方。
peopleEn: Arzawa appears in the documents chiefly through the title of its king, and the record preserves very few identifiable individuals. What is certain is Hattusili I of the Old Kingdom: it is in his campaign poem, the Song of Release, that the sack of Hapala and the union of Arzawa with the tribes of Assuwa are set down, and that poem remains the principal text through which this tradition of revolt can be reconstructed; his predecessor Muttallu I had drained the kingdom's strength on the eastern front against the Hurrians. At the other end stand the kings of Ugarit, among them Yaqarum, whose name appears in the palace letters of the late 13th century BC as he pressed his case in writing with Hatti and with Arzawa alike; those letters also mention Ahhiyawa, the kingdom of the Mycenaeans, and the king of Arzawa, which shows that the insurgents were not alone. On the Egyptian side the pharaoh in 1315 BC was Horemheb, reigning from 1319 to 1294 BC, and Seti I came after him; Egypt's attention was fixed on Canaan and the Sinai, and the early New Kingdom had not yet pushed its armies to the western Anatolian shore. Scholars still debate whether the heartland of Arzawa lay at Smyrna, at Ephesus, or higher up the Hermus valley, and that debate is itself the richest trace the uprising has left.
kits: 卡面這把埃及月牙劍是外彎的單刃短劍，砍進去不必拔出來，它在前1500年前後已是埃及步兵的制式裝備。但把卡面放到安納托利亞西部的戰場上，必須說清楚：這是一把外來兵器。在前1315年前後的安納托利亞，正規部隊裝備的是愛琴海—邁錫尼系統的直刃雙刃長劍，形制上帶中脊、柄頭作菱形或圓形，人稱「瑙埃二型」（Naue II）；此外是短劍、雙面青銅斧（阿爾薩瓦出土的斧頭沿用邁錫尼式雙刃，柄端穿孔繫繩）、尖頭長矛、投槍、短弓與石彈，以及投石索。防護上是圓盾與橢圓盾、繃皮或金屬盔，其中伊茲密出土的牛角盔與安納托利亞戰車最具辨識度；雙馬拉戰車由一名御者加一名射手同乘。埃及式鴨嘴刃在安納托利亞並不流行，但在迦南與西奈的考古層位中確實可見，說明它屬於東地中海的共享武備，而不是安納托利亞本地的主力兵器。
kitsEn: The khopesh on the card is a single-edged short sword with an outward bow, so that a blow did not have to be twisted out of the wound, and by around 1500 BC it was standard issue in the Egyptian infantry. Set the card down in western Anatolia, however, and it has to be said plainly: this is an imported weapon. In Anatolia around 1315 BC the regular troops carried the straight, double-edged swords of the Aegean and Mycenaean system, with a central rib and a lozenge-shaped or disc-shaped pommel, the type now called Naue II; alongside them were short swords, double-edged bronze axes (the axes recovered from Arzawa keep the Mycenaean double blade, with a perforated haft end for lashing), spearheads with leaf-shaped or triangular blades, javelins, short bows and sling-stones, and the sling itself. On the defensive side there were round and oval shields, leather or metal helmets, and among the most recognisable Anatolian finds the horned helmet and the war chariot; the two-horse chariot carried a driver and an archer side by side. The Egyptian duckbill blade was never at home in Anatolia, though it does turn up in the archaeological levels of Canaan and the Sinai, which places it in the shared armament of the eastern Mediterranean rather than among the main weapons of this battlefield.
tactics: 阿爾薩瓦聯盟的起事不像有統一指揮的正規會戰，更接近各城邦在同一季節各自舉兵的聯合作戰。西部安納托利亞多山，愛琴海沿岸的赫米斯河谷雖有可耕種的沖積平原，卻被山脈與松林切割，適合游騎與步兵分散作戰，不利於戰車展開；聯盟方因此避開赫梯遠征軍所長的開闊戰場，讓各部族依托山道、村寨與城牆作戰，拖住遠征軍的推進，同時用襲擊切斷赫梯在西部取得銀與鐵礦的通道。聯軍在作戰上並不協同：各城邦的守軍以土坯牆與石基牆固守，以投射武器與短兵在缺口抵抗，戰車多留作城內或用來嚇阻。赫梯方面的回應有固定套路：先以輕騎巡哨標定敵方聚落，再以國王親率的遠征軍自東面山脈越過愛琴海東岸逐村清剿，封住城外道路與渡口斷其糧援，最後迫使各城邦單獨議和，不給聯盟合流的時間。戰役多在春末夏初進行，因為這時道路可行、溪水未漲、穀物尚未收成，入冬前遠征軍必須撤回首都哈圖沙。
tacticsEn: The rising in Arzawa did not look like a set-piece battle with a unified command; it was closer to a set of city-states taking up arms in the same season. Western Anatolia is mountainous, and while the alluvial plain of the Hermus along the Aegean shore is cultivable it is cut up by ridges and pine forest, which suits skirmishing foot and light cavalry but gives no room for chariots to deploy. The allies therefore avoided the open ground on which a Hittite field army was strongest, and had the tribes fight from the tracks, villages and walls of their own country, slowing the column's advance while raiding cut off Hatti's access to silver and iron in the west. The coalition was not coordinated in the field: each town held behind its mud-brick and stone-block walls, meeting the assault with missiles and short weapons at the breaches, keeping its chariots inside the walls or using them only to overawe. Hatti's answer followed a fixed pattern: light cavalry scouted first and marked the enemy settlements, then the king's field army came over the hills from the east and worked through the settlements one by one, closing the roads and fords outside the towns to cut the grain, until each city was forced to make terms alone and the coalition was never given time to join up. Campaigns were fought in late spring and early summer, while the roads were still passable, the streams had not risen and the harvest was not yet in; before winter the field army had to be back at Hattusa.
data: 這場起義的可靠數字非常有限，可以確定的有以下幾組。其一，阿爾薩瓦聯盟的規模在赫梯老王國的詩篇裡以二十部族這樣的聯盟結構出現，詩中對各部族的殲滅多以數百人為單位記載，可見其為數十支部眾的鬆散集合，而不是一支集中的軍隊。其二，烏加里特王宮的泥板檔案在前13世紀末達到數千片的規模，其中提及阿爾薩瓦的信件屬於這批檔案；從安納托利亞西部沿海到烏加里特的王宮，走海路約需數百公里，走信使的陸海接力約一至三個月，這意味烏加里特的書信幾乎無法指揮安納托利亞內陸的戰事。其三，前1315年前後的東地中海並非真空：埃及仍在迦南與西奈用兵，赫梯正準備把陣線推向奧龍特斯河與幼發拉底河，任何西部起事都發生在雙方互相牽制的背景下。至於前1315年那一年究竟出動多少人、交戰多久、以何方式收場，沒有任何一份當時的戰報留下數字；本文所記月份與部署，是依安納托利亞的遠征季節與地形所作的重建。
dataEn: Reliable figures for this rising are few, and only the following groups can be established. First, the size of the Arzawa coalition appears in the Old Kingdom poems as a structure of twenty tribes, and the poems reckon the destruction of those tribes in units of several hundred men, which shows a loose gathering of dozens of contingents rather than a concentrated army. Second, the clay-tablet archive of the royal palace at Ugarit reached several thousand pieces by the late 13th century BC, and the letters naming Arzawa belong to that archive; the run from the western Anatolian coast to the royal court at Ugarit was several hundred kilometres by sea and one to three months by the relay of messengers, which means the Ugaritic correspondence could barely direct fighting in the Anatolian interior. Third, the eastern Mediterranean around 1315 BC was not a vacuum: Egypt was still campaigning in Canaan and the Sinai and Hatti was preparing to push its line towards the Orontes and the Euphrates, and any rising in the west therefore happened against a background of mutual entanglement between the two powers. As for how many men were committed in 1315 BC, how long the fighting lasted, and in what way it ended, no contemporary report gives a single number; the month and the deployments given here are a reconstruction from the Anatolian campaigning season and the terrain.
cause: 把這場起義推向前1315年前後，可以從三條線索看起。第一是宗主關係的成本：阿爾薩瓦在哈圖西里一世之後是赫梯的附庸，須繳納銀與銅、供應木材與兵員，而在赫梯把主力投入敘利亞與埃及戰線的年代，西部的徵發常常跟不上需要，附庸的負擔與宗主給予的保護不成比例。第二是資源的誘惑：安納托利亞西部是銅、銀與早期鐵的來源地，愛琴海東岸的城邦各自控制著礦點與冶煉場，阿爾薩瓦若能擺脫赫梯的徵調，便能自己把礦產換成財富。第三是身份與競爭：赫梯王國的邊疆從未真正整合西部，盧維亞語與胡里安語的地名、人名在阿爾薩瓦各地並行，那裡的人與東面使用印歐語系的赫梯人並非同一族群；同時阿赫伊瓦的商船隊正沿著海岸北上，把阿爾薩瓦變成通往米諾斯與邁錫尼的跳板。三條線索疊在一起，就出現了一種典型的起義邏輯：名義上仍承認宗主，實際上把徵稅、徵兵與貿易的控制收回自己手裡。
causeEn: Three threads can be followed into the years around 1315 BC. The first is the cost of the overlordship: after Hattusili I, Arzawa was a vassal of Hatti and had to render silver and copper, timber and men, and in the years when Hatti's main effort lay in Syria and Egypt the levies demanded from the west repeatedly outran what the lord could give in return, so the burden of the vassal and the protection it received no longer matched. The second is the temptation of resources: western Anatolia was a source of copper, silver and of the earliest iron, and the Aegean-side city-states each held mines and smelting floors of their own, so a shaken-off Arzawa could turn its ore into wealth on its own terms. The third is identity and rivalry: the Hittite state had never truly integrated the west, and Luwian and Hurrian place-names and personal names ran in parallel through Arzawa, among people who were not one people with the Indo-European Hittites to their east; at the same time the trading ships of Ahhiyawa were working north along the coast, turning Arzawa into a stepping-stone towards Minoan and Mycenaean shores. Where the three overlap lies a typical logic of revolt: the overlord is still acknowledged in name, while the levies, the taxes and the control of trade are quietly taken back into local hands.
impact: 這場起義在當時的直接結果，是赫梯王國的西部邊境在整個前13世紀都沒有真正安寧。赫梯不得不反覆從東線抽調兵馬，把遠征軍的成本一次又一次壓在阿爾薩瓦與其鄰近諸邦身上；阿爾薩瓦的核心地區在此後數百年裡逐漸被卡西人吸收，赫梯西線的邊界由固定的城塞退化成難以防守的山地界線，王國必須用阿爾薩瓦問題這種持久性威脅，來不斷消耗本已緊張的資源。更長遠的一層，是青銅時代晚期的整個西地中海秩序：阿爾薩瓦的港口與內陸道路是愛琴海東岸移民與商人往來的走廊，東邊的烏加里特把它當作上游供應地，西邊的阿赫伊瓦把它當作進入安納托利亞的跳板，這種多重身分讓它在城邦崩潰的年代格外脆弱——前13世紀末烏加里特王宮被焚、前12世紀赫梯王國的崩解，都發生在這條走廊上。考古上，阿爾薩瓦的物質文化是安納托利亞與愛琴海風格交界處的標誌，也正是十九世紀以來學者爭論其核心地帶的依據。
impactEn: The immediate effect of this rising was that the western frontier of the Hittite kingdom was never quiet for the whole of the 13th century BC. Hatti had repeatedly to draw troops away from the eastern front and charged the cost of each campaign once more onto Arzawa and its neighbours; the core of Arzawa was gradually absorbed in the centuries that followed by the Kaska, and the Hittite western frontier shrank from a line of fixed fortresses into a barely defensible mountain border, so that the kingdom had to spend an enduring threat called the Arzawa question on resources that were already strained. On the longer view the effect belongs to the whole late Bronze Age order in the western Mediterranean: the ports and inland roads of Arzawa were the corridor along which settlers and traders moved between the Aegean and the east, with Ugarit treating it as a source of upstream supply to the east and Ahhiyawa treating it as a landing place on the road into Anatolia to the west, and that multiple identity made it especially exposed in the age of the city-states' collapse — the burning of the palace at Ugarit at the end of the 13th century BC and the disintegration of the Hittite kingdom in the 12th century both happened along this corridor. Archaeologically the material culture of Arzawa marks the seam between the Anatolian and the Aegean styles, and it is the evidence on which the debate over the heartland has been fought since the nineteenth century.
result: 以傳統戰爭年表的說法，這一場以阿爾薩瓦聯盟被壓服收場：赫梯重新取得西部附庸的徵稅與軍事義務，安納托利亞西岸回到宗主秩序之下。但就史料而言，結果其實沒有這樣整齊。沒有任何一份公元前十四世紀的文件記載過公元前1315年的一場戰鬥、損失表或俘獲名單；阿爾薩瓦起義這個名目，本身就是把三個不同年代的材料壓縮成的傳統名稱——蘇美爾與阿卡德時期阿爾薩瓦地區反覆叛離阿卡德的舊事、赫梯老王國詩篇裡哈帕拉被毀的那一次遠征，以及前13世紀烏加里特信件中阿爾薩瓦與周邊城邦往來糾葛的日常。若只取其最後一層，結果並非臣服：阿爾薩瓦並未從烏加里特與阿赫伊瓦的往來中退場，它在信件中仍然以獨立的國王與獨立的軍隊出現，直到前13世紀末的崩潰把它與整個西亞的舊秩序一起帶走。赫梯贏得的是一段不靠條約、不靠戰報維持的秩序；而那把卡面上的埃及月牙劍，則提醒我們這場衝突始終發生在同一個東地中海的武備循環裡。
resultEn: On the traditional war chronology the affair ended with the Arzawa coalition put down: Hatti recovered the right to draw tribute and military service from its western vassal, and the Aegean coast of Anatolia was returned to the overlord's order. On the evidence, however, the result was not so tidy. No document of the fourteenth century BC records a battle, a casualty list or a roster of prisoners from 1315 BC; the name Arzawa revolt is itself a traditional compression of material from three different periods — the older memory of Arzawa's repeated defection from Akkad in the Sumerian and Akkadian age, the one Hittite campaign in the Old Kingdom poem that ends with the destruction of Hapala, and the day-to-day friction of Arzawa's dealings with its neighbours in the Ugaritic letters of the 13th century BC. Take only the last layer, and the result is not submission: Arzawa did not drop out of its dealings with Ugarit and Ahhiyawa, and in the letters it still appears with its own king and its own troops, until the collapse at the end of the 13th century BC carried it away together with the whole old order of western Asia. What Hatti won was an order maintained without a treaty and without a report; and the Egyptian khopesh on the card is a reminder that the whole conflict took place inside a single armament circuit of the eastern Mediterranean.
